Milestone: Choose a Pygame theme and agree the shared brief
Activity: Compare two themes, select one and map all common functional/non-functional requirements to a player need. Keep the same game core for every theme.
Evidence check: Explain the scope and exclusions; show the prerequisite preparation record before project issue.

Milestone: Design game states, functions and one-dimensional lists
Activity: Design title/play/pause/result states, function interfaces, collectible-list records, patrols, score history and normal/challenge settings. Desk-check win/loss precedence and predicted tests.
Evidence check: Design checkpoint: explain pause/reset, once-only collection, file policy and independent expected results.

Milestone: Build the game state and controls skeleton
Activity: Use the selected scenario shell and supplied fixtures. Implement initial state, documented controls, pause/resume/restart/quit and separate update/draw responsibilities.
Evidence check: Demonstrate start and restart returning score, lives, time and objects to their required initial values.

Milestone: Build movement and fixed-layout collision rules
Activity: Implement four-direction movement and bounds, then collection and hazard consequences in small testable functions. Use primitive shapes before decorative assets.
Evidence check: Checkpoint: explain a movement boundary test and show one collectible scores only once.

Milestone: Implement score, lives and active-play timing
Activity: Integrate five collectibles, three deterministic hazards, safe respawn and 1000 ms protection. Resolve loss before win and keep paused time out of the active timer.
Evidence check: Trace two hits at the protection boundary and verify the zero-time/exit collision outcome.

Milestone: Implement the HUD and score-history functions
Activity: Show controls/score/lives/time and shape/text distinctions. Append the final score once, load valid history and compute count, total and first maximum position.
Evidence check: Build checkpoint: test a repeated result update, missing/empty history, malformed lines and a failed write policy.

Milestone: Integrate difficulty choices and the complete game core
Activity: Integrate the two fixed patrol intervals, all states and history report. Preserve all other rules and primitive fallbacks. Prepare a known-good version for testing.
Evidence check: Demonstrate normal 1000 ms and challenge 750 ms patrol intervals without changing scoring, item counts or time.

Milestone: Run the common game tests, repair and retest
Activity: Use the shared acceptance cases plus function tests. Record expected and actual results, isolate faults and rerun failed and previously passing cases.
Evidence check: Show pause, restart, collision/timer, history and quality evidence; leave unrun checks pending.

Milestone: Conduct the player acceptance and quality trial
Activity: Ask a peer to use only the instructions. Check usability, non-colour cues, offline paths, reliability and the named-machine response target. Record feedback and retests.
Evidence check: Match observations to NFR IDs; distinguish measured results from intended behaviour.

Milestone: Demonstrate, evaluate and hand over the game
Activity: Explain student-authored functions/list/file processing, restore a saved version, evaluate every common requirement and complete the retrospective/source/asset log.
Evidence check: Hand over the selected theme, code, fixtures, workbook and test evidence under the school-issued conditions.
